show_hn.story_text: Howdy HN! Missing a fast pure Go embedded SQL database. The issue is that compared to C, go is slow. Having done a lot of JIT in go, I naturally wanted to stick a JIT that generates native query kernels and see what happens. Result: musql. Pronounced "muscle." On a 100K-row filtered count, musql takes 21 µs: about 300x faster than C SQLite and nearly 1,000x faster than Turso. Single-threaded, warm cache, using musql's direct API, native C SQLite, and Turso's Go driver. Filtered sums are 130x faster than C SQLite, grouped aggregates 95x. It works with Go's database/sql or through a server for libSQL clients. It uses its own storage format, with SQLite import/export. And yes, the SQL VM runs DOOM. show_hn.story_text: I always wanted to create my own programming language. Sometimes, when I was bored, I would open my computer and start improvising one (in C# on OnlineGDB, because Visual Studio is so heavy and I only open it for serious projects), but I always abandoned it after a few minutes when I realized I didn't even know how to begin. I didn't want to follow a tutorial or anything. I wanted to figure it out myself. I didn't know what a parser was, what a lexer was, what a syntax tree was, or even what an interpreter was. My mindset was basically: "I want to write a program that gets a string containing code and does what it says."
